chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madai'ni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: (And does not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord)

He said: It is the servant who performs an act of worship without seeking the pleasure of Allah; rather, he only seeks the commendation of people, desiring to be heard of. This is the one who associates others in the worship of his Lord.

And he said: There is no servant who hides a good [deed] and days go by, but that Allah manifests good for him; and there is no servant who hides an evil [deed] and days pass, but that Allah will manifest evil for him.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'associating anyone in the worship of his Lord' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse 'And do not associate with your Lord anyone' (18:110) by identifying *riya'* (showing off) as the specific form of minor shirk where one performs righteous deeds for human acclaim rather than divine pleasure. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of intention (*ikhlas*) as the cornerstone of valid worship. The Imam further links this to the principle of divine reciprocity, noting that concealed good deeds yield hidden blessings, while concealed sins bring about corresponding divine retribution.
